public_rationale: The firm claim predicts eventual AGI; its century reference is tentative. Recent independent testing shows a major capability milestone, but the evaluator explicitly stops short of calling it AGI. No located evidence meets the decisive-event rule. Nor can elapsed time disprove an eventual-achievement forecast.
limitations: AGI definitions differ, and selecting one can change whether an achievement qualifies.
The search cannot establish that no qualifying private system exists.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Humanity will eventually reach AGI, quite possibly before the end of the 21st century.
public_payload.original_horizon_text: before the end of this century

statement.excerpt: I do think we will eventually reach AGI (artificial general intelligence), and quite possibly before the end of this century.
statement.document_title: AGI will not happen in your lifetime. Or will it?

from_speaker: quite possibly before the end of this century
our_interpretation: The firm prediction is eventual achievement. 'Quite possibly' expresses a possibility before the century ends, not a commitment to that deadline.
Accordingly, the firm forecast has an open horizon. The century reference would extend through 2100-12-31 if treated as a deadline, but that would strengthen his wording.
Read AGI as flexible, reliable general intelligence comparable to humans, rather than success on a single benchmark.
criteria.support_condition: A dated, independently substantiated achievement demonstrates human-comparable general intelligence across substantially different domains and unfamiliar tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence establishes that the predicted achievement cannot ever occur. Failure to achieve it by an arbitrarily selected date is insufficient.

evidence.excerpt: GPT-6 Astra surpasses the human baseline in action efficiency on ARC-AGI-3.
evidence.explanation: This is substantial evidence of progress on unfamiliar interactive tasks. The same report limits the benchmark to closed environments and explicitly declines to identify Astra as AGI, so it does not meet the resolution rule.

evidence.excerpt: There is no generally accepted empirical test for AGI.
evidence.explanation: The assessment compares recent AGI declarations with several proposed tests and identifies missing evaluations. It does not establish a conclusive achievement or prove that AGI is impossible.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated achievement independently demonstrating flexible, reliable human-comparable general intelligence across domains; alternatively, decisive evidence that such achievement is impossible.
